_comment: Navigation sweep profile for Lemmings (NES, Sunsoft 1993) - ADR-0239's own
scope, s6: 'a sixth game is a profile, not a code change'. No new PRD slice
is claimed for it. Read by scripts/record_navigation_sweep.py.
RUNG 1, NOT RUNG 2. ADR-0239 s1 says to use the first rung that reaches the
place, and for this ROM that is rung 1: the game's own selector, by input.
navigation.kind is 'input', so no cheat rides with any session and every
session is an ADR-0184 s2 'clean' pass that all four surfaces may read. Rung
2 is not available and was checked first: there is no published RAM map for
this port. The two maps that exist for Lemmings are for the Amiga original,
and this port's level list, its level layout and its access codes are its
own (Sunsoft/Ocean ported the Amiga levels, but the NES build stores its own
100-entry table). A RAM selector would need an invented address, which
ADR-0184 s5 refuses.
THE SELECTOR. The title screen takes Start after ~900 frames and opens the
main menu - START / NEW LEVEL / FUN / a music toggle - which is a pointer,
not a cursor: the D-pad moves a lemming-shaped arrow and A clicks it. With
Right once the arrow sits on NEW LEVEL and A opens 'ENTER YOUR ACCESS CODE /
THEN PUSH START BUTTON', six characters wide over six ASCII bytes at
$0054-$0059 in internal RAM. Start submits; the game answers on the same
screen with 'CODE IS FOR LEVEL n / RATING IS x' about 150 frames later; a
second Start opens the level's preview ('LEVEL n', the title, NUMBER OF
LEMMINGS / NUMBER TO BE SAVED / RELEASE RATE / TIME); a third Start begins
play. The answer screen times out back to the menu after a few seconds, so
the entry script presses Start twice more inside the same run rather than
leaving a gap.
THE ALPHABET AND THE TYPING RULE. The screen cycles 21 letters,
BCDFGHJKLMNPQRSTVWXYZ - the vowels are not in it, which is also exactly the
letter set all 100 codes are drawn from. B is index 0, the value every
position opens on, which is why the screen shows BBBBBB. Up increments the
character under the cursor and Right moves the cursor; A and B do nothing;
Start submits. Up is an autorepeat whose counter is NOT reset on release: a
hold of k frames advances the character by k // 8 and the remainder carries
into the next hold, so a hold of 8 * index advances exactly index steps and
leaves the counter at zero. Measured on this dump both ways - a single hold
of 8/16/24/32/48/64/96 frames advanced 1/2/3/4/6/8/12 steps (B, C, D, F, J,
L, Q), and four 10-frame holds separated by 120 frames advanced 5 steps, not
4, because the 2 leftover frames per hold accumulate.
scripts/stages/lemmings/access-code.py turns that into the six presses per
code, and each character's buffer byte was read back out of a save state to
confirm the transcription (16 of 16 codes typed byte for byte,
runs/f1417/lemmings/probe/*/s.mss).
WHERE THE CODES COME FROM. This ROM's own level table, at PRG offset 0x1964
of this dump: 100 records, each '<6 ASCII letters><release rate> <level-data
bank><title>\0', contiguous with no gaps. The release rate is the byte the
game itself prints on the preview (all 16 below read back equal,
probe/preview-sheet.png) and the second byte is a bank in 0xA0-0xAB, 17
distinct values over the 100 records. Record n is level n - the game itself
says so: typing record 2's code (TYRNVD) makes the game print 'CODE IS FOR
LEVEL 2 / RATING IS FUN', and record 76's code (SJFHGD) 'CODE IS FOR LEVEL 1
/ RATING IS MAYHEM' (the number it prints is the index INSIDE the rating;
see the RAM check below). Nothing here is invented: the source is the game's
own data, read off this dump, and every one of the 16 codes below was then
accepted by the game itself and its level preview captured
(runs/f1417/lemmings/probe/PV2-*/mesen-home/ Screenshots, 16 of 16).
A community table was looked for first and could not be reached from this
environment: Data Crystal and TCRF serve a JavaScript challenge
(datacrystal.tcrf.net/wiki/Lemmings_(NES), tcrf.net/Lemmings_(NES)),
GameFAQs and CheatCC answer 'Just a moment' and refuse a text-extraction
proxy, Neoseeker serves a security check, and lemmingsuniverse.net's codes
page lists Amiga, PC, Mac, C64, 3DO and Oh No! More Lemmings but no NES
entry. The ROM's own table is a stronger source than any of them would have
been, and it is checkable by anyone holding the dump.
THE RAM CHECK, AND WHAT IT PROVES. The game keeps the level as two
consequence bytes: $00A1 is the rating (0 Fun, 1 Tricky, 2 Taxing, 3 Mayhem)
and $00A0 is the index inside that rating (0-24), so the flat level is $00A1
* 25 + $00A0 + 1. Measured, not assumed: 27 save states, one per level
probed, every one reads its own pair (runs/f1417/lemmings/ probe,
unversioned), and the game's own screens agree - the preview of level 51
prints 'LEVEL 1' while $00A0 reads 00, the preview of level 100 prints
'LEVEL 25' while $00A0 reads 18 hex = 24, and the answer screen of level 76
prints 'CODE IS FOR LEVEL 1 / RATING IS MAYHEM' while the pair reads (3, 0).
Each value's ramCheck names $00A0 alone, because a ramCheck is one address.
$00A0 is the byte the level loader sets to the place, and it is what catches
a session that drifts: if the level ends and the game moves on, the byte
moves with it. It does NOT separate two values of different ratings that
happen to sit at the same index (level 5 and level 30 are both index 4),
which is why the pair, and the table of pairs, is written down here rather
than only the expected byte. Neither byte is pinned - this profile carries
no cheat at all - so ADR-0239 s4's caveat about a pin substituting on the
read bus does not arise for any session here.
WHY LEVEL 1 IS NOT A VALUE. Level 1 (code XSQWRJ, 'JUST DIG') is what the
game's own stage-1 route reaches - title, menu, click START - and that route
is this sweep's 'before' side (ADR-0239 s5). A session that recorded level 1
under its code would add nothing the baseline does not already hold and
would read as did-not-warp. The same reason Ninja Gaiden's profile leaves
Act 1-1 out. The code itself is kept in that profile's notes rather than in
values[].
THE 16 VALUES, and why these. All four ratings are covered (6 Fun, 4 Tricky,
3 Taxing, 3 Mayhem) and so are the art families the port draws from, counted
by reading a frame of each level: the Roman/gold set (2, 13, 51, 90), the
teal steel lattice (5, 30, 48, 70), red brick with magenta (4, 40, 85), grey
brick with fire (17, 60), the blue faceted crystal (100), red-brown rock
with fire (12) and dirt with moss (26). Seven families over 16 values.
Levels 1, 3, 16, 22, 35, 45, 55, 65, 76, 95 were also probed and are not
swept - they repeat a family or a rating the 16 already carry (level 1 is
also the baseline above).
THAT LIST IS A CORRECTION, and the record of it is the frames. The first
pass of tags was read off the 120 s probes in probe/L*/ and in five of them
the frame had landed on the level's own fail screen, so the tag described
whatever was on screen rather than the level. Re-reading a level-start frame
for those five (probe/start-sheet.png) regrouped the set: level 2 is the
Roman/gold set and not 'brick', level 26 is dirt, level 40 is red brick with
magenta rather than 'blue stone', level 51 is Roman/gold rather than 'grey
stone', 90 is Roman/gold rather than 'gold/red pillar', and 5, 30 and 48 are
one teal lattice rather than 'crystal and ice' - which leaves 100 as the
only crystal level swept. values[]._artFrame carries the reading and names
its sheet.
THE STAGE-CLEAR TRANSITION IS NEVER RECORDED by any session here, exactly as
ADR-0239 s6 and ADR-0184's 2026-09-14 amendment say: the selector is input,
so what the run records is the level it was typed into and whatever the
blind body does inside it. Deaths and retries are recorded - the body
presses A, which is TRY AGAIN on the 'ALL LEMMINGS ACCOUNTED FOR' screen, so
a level lost inside the run replays instead of parking on the fail screen
(ADR-0184 s4 is met: the level's own fail screen is on the record). What no
pack holds is the frames between one level and the next.
NO LIVES PIN, so ADR-0239 s3's inert control does not apply. Lemmings has no
lives counter: the run's unit is the level, a level that fails offers TRY
AGAIN, and no GAME OVER screen exists for a pin to foreclose.
defaults.cheats is therefore absent, and no process in this sweep is
launched with a cheat at all.
NO stage-set.json IN THIS FOLDER, deliberately. The unattended library job
matches a ROM to a folder only through that file, and this folder is a sweep
profile: mint-stage1.txt starts the game's default route and
mint-level-*.txt type a code, while stage1-run.txt is the play loop the sweep
repeats - none of the three is a route the job should record on its own.
stage1-run.txt is the run from the state mint-stage1.txt mints - the
README's own mint/run pair - so the job records a real route and not the
title screen. The ROM is declared: see stage-set.json.
_provenanceComment: romSha1 is the No-Intro SHA1 of the library dump this profile was authored
and recorded on (scripts/mep_build.py's _no_intro_sha1). The whole-file SHA1
of the same dump is 62E587CE49FF641FAC3BE1E6268D21038212D0FA, which is the
swap byte range between the two; iNES header CRC32 0xCB2C08D4, mapper 1
(MMC1B2, NES-SLROM), 8 PRG banks and 16 CHR banks, so this is a CHR ROM game
and ADR-0239 s5.2 has a denominator for it. The ROM is the user's own dump
and is never copied into the repository.

navigation.label: the title menu's NEW LEVEL entry, which opens the ACCESS CODE screen ('ENTER YOUR ACCESS CODE / THEN PUSH START BUTTON')
navigation.source: This ROM's own behaviour, read off this dump 2026-09-26 (screens under runs/f1417/lemmings/probe, unversioned), and the 100-entry access-code table the ROM carries at PRG offset 0x1964 - six ASCII letters, a release rate and a null-terminated title per record, record n being level n. An entry script types one code: the access-code screen's 21-letter alphabet (BCDFGHJKLMNPQRSTVWXYZ, the vowels absent), Up advancing one step per 8 held frames from B, Right moving the cursor, Start submitting and Start opening the preview and beginning play. ADR-0239 s1 rung 1: input, no cheat. Read by scripts/record_navigation_sweep.py; the per-code press sequences are generated by scripts/stages/lemmings/access-code.py.

_defaultsComment: entry is the game's own stage-1 route (title -> menu -> click START -> the
LEVEL 1 preview -> play), which is what the sweep's 'before' side records
under runs/f1417/lemmings/before/ (ADR-0239 s5). No value here uses it -
every value names its own entry script, because a code is what selects the
level - but it is kept so the file stays a valid profile for a value added
later, and because level 1 really is reached by that path.
seconds is ADR-0239 s6's budget. The body is stage1-run.txt: the cursor is the
view in this port, so it pans a long way in each direction, and it taps A -
assign during play, TRY AGAIN on the fail screen - so a level the blind body
loses replays inside the run instead of leaving the session on the fail
screen. B is never pressed: on the fail screen B returns to the menu.
No lives pin rides with a code: the entry is input, not a cheat, so ADR-0239
s3 does not apply and the game's own fail screen stays on the record
